Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

derivations.claim: The string components. $V_{2\omega}=\mathbb Q(q)v_2$ with $E_1v_2=0$, so the decomposition of $v_2$ is $v_2=F_1^{(0)}v_2$ with top component $v_2\in H_{2\omega}$. Since $v_1=F_1v_2=F_1^{(1)}v_2$ and $V_0=\mathbb Q(q)v_1$, the decomposition of $v_1$ is $v_1=F_1^{(1)}v_2$ with top component $v_2\in H_{2\omega}$; likewise $v_0=F_1^{(2)}v_2$ is the decomposition of $v_0$ with top component $v_2\in H_{2\omega}$.

The six formulas. Reading the definitions off the decompositions of step 1.1: $\tilde e_1v_2=0$, $\tilde e_1v_1=F_1^{(0)}v_2=v_2$, $\tilde e_1v_0=F_1^{(1)}v_2=v_1$ and $\tilde f_1v_2=F_1^{(1)}v_2=v_1$, $\tilde f_1v_1=F_1^{(2)}v_2=v_0$, $\tilde f_1v_0=F_1^{(3)}v_2=0$. In particular $F_1v_1=[2]_1v_0$ while $\tilde f_1v_1=v_0$, and $E_1v_0=v_1=\tilde e_1v_0$ and $F_1v_0=0=\tilde f_1v_0$ show the bottom agreements; the interior difference is exactly the factor $[2]_1\neq1$.

Lattice and residue basis. Since $v_2,v_1,v_0$ have distinct weights, $\mathcal L(2\omega)=A_0v_2\oplus A_0v_1\oplus A_0v_0$ and it generates $V$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$; step 2.1 shows that $\tilde e_1$ and $\tilde f_1$ preserve it, so it is a crystal lattice. The classes $b_2,b_1,b_0$ of the three basis vectors are $\mathbb Q$-independent in $L/qL$ because $L$ is free with those basis vectors and the crystal-limit map is an isomorphism, so they form a $\mathbb Q$-basis; the operator action of step 2.1 lies in $\{b_2,b_1,b_0\}\cup\{0\}$, and the only nonzero arrows are $b_2\to b_1$ and $b_1\to b_0$, whose inverses under $\tilde e_1$ hold, giving the partial-inverse axiom.

The invariants. From the chain $b_2\to b_1\to b_0$ the values $\varepsilon_1(b_2)=0$, $\varepsilon_1(b_1)=1$, $\varepsilon_1(b_0)=2$ and $\varphi_1(b_2)=2$, $\varphi_1(b_1)=1$, $\varphi_1(b_0)=0$ are immediate, and the weights are those of step 3.1; the equalities $\varphi_1(b)=\varepsilon_1(b)+\langle h_1,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle$ read $2=0+2$, $1=1+0$, $0=2-2$.

Partial inverses. Evaluating step 2.1 gives $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_2=v_2$, $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_1=v_1$, $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_0=0=v_0-p_{\mathrm{bot}}v_0$, and $\tilde f_1\tilde e_1v_2=0=v_2-p_0v_2$, $\tilde f_1\tilde e_1v_1=v_1=v_1-p_0v_1$, $\tilde f_1\tilde e_1v_0=v_0=v_0-p_0v_0$; by linearity these are the stated identities, and no choice is used because everything is computed on the three displayed vectors.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

We also write $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ for the datum's integer pairing $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: The negative-half crystal. By [F1], the divided monomials $F_1^{(n)}$ form a field basis of the polynomial algebra, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}A_0F_1^{(n)}$. Reducing this free direct sum modulo $q$ shows that the residue classes $b_n=F_1^{(n)}+q\mathcal L(\infty)$ ($n\ge0$) are nonzero and linearly independent modulo $q$; the operators act as $\tilde f_1b_n=b_{n+1}$ and $\tilde e_1b_{n+1}=b_n$, $\tilde e_1b_0=0$. Hence $\mathcal B(\infty)\cong\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, with weights $\mathrm{wt}(b_n)=-n\alpha_1=-2n\omega$, $\varepsilon_1(b_n)=n$, formal $\varphi_1(b_n)=n-2n=-n$ and $\ell_1^-(b_n)=\infty$.

The module crystal. By [F2], $\pi_m(F_1^{(n)})=v_n$ for $n\le m$ and $0$ for $n>m$; so $\pi_m(b_n)=0$ for $n>m$ and $\pi_m(b_n)=v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ for $0\le n\le m$. The classes $v_0,\dots,v_m$ are a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(m\omega)/q\mathcal L(m\omega)$, and the operator action on them is the string action, so the surviving residues map bijectively onto $\mathcal B(m\omega)$; this is (a).

Raising compatibility and its failure. For $0\le n\le m$ one has $\tilde e_1\pi_m(b_n)=\tilde e_1(v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega))=v_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ and $0$ for $n=0$, while $\pi_m(\tilde e_1b_n)=v_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ and $0$ for $n=0$; hence the two sides agree for every surviving residue. At the killed residue $n=m+1$, the left side is $\tilde e_1\pi_m(b_{m+1})=\tilde e_1\cdot0=0$, while the right side is $\pi_m(\tilde e_1b_{m+1})=\pi_m(b_m)=v_m\neq0$ modulo $q$; this is the stated boundary failure. Lowering: $\tilde f_1\pi_m(b_n)=v_{n+1}$ for $n<m$ and $0$ for $n\ge m$, while $\pi_m(\tilde f_1b_n)=v_{n+1}$ for $n<m$ and $0$ for $n\ge m$, so both sides agree for every $n$.

Isomorphism in fixed degree. In root degree $-n\alpha_1$ the free $A_0$-module $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-n\alpha_1}$ is the one-dimensional span of $F_1^{(n)}$ with residue $b_n$, and $\mathcal L(m\omega)_{m\omega-n\alpha_1}$ is the one-dimensional span of $v_n$ with residue $v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ for $m\ge n$; the map $\pi_m$ sends $F_1^{(n)}$ to $v_n$, an isomorphism on these one-dimensional free modules, and its surviving-residue set is $\{b_n\}$ when $m\ge n$ and empty otherwise. Together with step 3.1 this is the large-weight instance of the projection lemma.

Choice. The computations of steps 1.1 through 4.1 use only explicit monomials, divided powers and one-dimensional free modules, so they are choice-free; the axiom of choice is declared because the cited general suppliers [F3] inherit it from the grand loop.

boundaries.evidence: The case $m=0$ kills every $b_n$ with $n>0$ and leaves the singleton surviving set $\{b_0\}$: step 2.1's bijection maps it onto the one-dimensional crystal $\mathcal B(0)$ of the trivial module, and step 4.1's degree isomorphism is the identity on the degree-zero component $A_0$.

The killed residues are exactly $\pi_m(b_n)=0$ for $n>m$ by step 2.1; on the negative half no $\tilde f_1$-image vanishes, since $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1=\operatorname{id}$ in step 1.1, and the zero value of $\tilde e_1$ occurs only at the top $b_0$.

The case $m=1$: the surviving residues $\{b_0,b_1\}$ map onto the two-vertex crystal of $V(\omega)$, and the failure of raising first appears at $b_2$, where $\pi_1(b_2)=0$ while $\pi_1(\tilde e_1b_2)=v_1\ne0$ by step 3.1.

The negative-half crystal is the degenerate infinite-string case: step 1.1 records the formal $\varphi_1(b_n)=-n$, negative for $n\ge1$ and not a chain length, together with $\ell_1^-=\infty$; this is exactly the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition and is kept separate from the module crystals.

The endpoint of the surviving range is $n=m+1$: step 3.1 shows that raising fails exactly there, while lowering commutes for every $n$, and step 4.1 identifies the degree isomorphism on the one-dimensional components for $m\ge n$ and the empty surviving fibre for $m<n$.

Step 5.1 records that the computations of steps 1.1 through 4.1 use only explicit monomials, divided powers and one-dimensional free modules and are choice-free; the axiom of choice is declared only because the cited general suppliers [F3] inherit it from the grand loop.

The bijection of (a) is proved in step 2.1 from both sides: forward, the classes $\pi_m(b_n)=v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ for $0\le n\le m$ are distinct because the residue basis $\{v_0,\dots,v_m\}$ is linearly independent, so the map is injective onto its image.

Reverse reading of the same step 2.1: every residue $v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ of $\mathcal B(m\omega)$ is the image of the surviving class $b_n$, so the map is surjective onto $\mathcal B(m\omega)$; together with the killed classes $n>m$ the two directions give the stated bijection.
